label: Contained in a bearer: the item is an intrinsic determination of the bearer
term: contained in a bearer (Contains b e)
definition: Contains b e: the item e is contained in the bearer b, as an intrinsic determination or as the bearer's own nature, not as a separate being. Containment may be intentional (an idea, the form of another as other) or virtual (a power to produce, a mode in which the bearer's nature is imitable); the relation does not say which. Examples: an idea in a mind; a disposition of a body; the one nature of a simple source. Non-examples: an abstract object that exists whether or not the bearer does; a product the bearer has made outside itself. Structural properties: a declared primitive two-place relation; it implies neither apprehension nor production.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 premise lane C), attribution deferred. See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Individuating non-present candidates: the axiarchic rival and the cognition criterion'. Lean has no declaration for it: it is the parameter Contains : B → C → Prop. That intentional and virtual containment are not separated in the type is deliberate: the containment-recognition bridge is exactly the step between them.
